recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless MnM later chooses to reword the already-applied Timing.code definition.
issue_request: FHIR-12402 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes issue asking how to express a Timing code such as BID together with start and stop bounds. The accepted resolution was to document that repeat.bounds still applies while the rest of repeat is an equivalent representation of the code that may be ignored or processed instead of the code.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 11150, represented in git as 238d8f7725591c1b0622e20dd50e36395feb3197, which changed source/datatypes/timing.sheet.txt and source/datatypes/timing.xml to add the repeat.bounds exception to the Timing.code definition. The old sheet text was later removed, but the active source/datatypes/timing.xml retained the rule.
additional_context: Timing is active in source/fhir.ini as a datatype, maps to the datatypes page, is marked normative, and has abbreviation tim. Bounded Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision; Jira concept hits concerned other Timing bounds or example issues rather than the relationship between Timing.code and Timing.repeat.bounds.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Timing.code definition says that either the code or structured data may be used to interpret the Timing, with the exception that .repeat.bounds still applies over the code and is not contained in the code.
